question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
answer: To be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in a course, you must maintain a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in that course. This requirement is calculated separately for both the theory and practical components of the course.

question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
answer: For a theory course, "Every theory course is evaluated for 100 marks, of which 40 marks are allotted to continuous internal assessment and 60 marks to the end-semester examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations."

question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
answer: To pass a course you "must secure a minimum of 30 per cent of the marks in the end-semester examination and a minimum of 40 per cent of the total marks, that is, the internal assessment and the end-semester examination taken together." A student who fails to satisfy either requirement will be awarded the grade "F".

question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
answer: If you obtain 85 marks, you will be awarded the A+ (Excellent) letter grade. According to the grading table, the A+ grade corresponds to a range of 80 to 89 marks.

question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
answer: You may apply for re-evaluation of the answer script for a theory course "within ten working days of the declaration of results, on payment of the prescribed fee per course". No application shall be entertained after this period.

question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
answer: If you miss an end-semester examination due to illness, you must submit a medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner and countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer to the Controller of Examinations within five working days. Once the certificate is accepted, you will be permitted to take the course in the next supplementary examination. This appearance will be treated as your first attempt and will be exempt from the supplementary examination fee.

question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the examination hall, possession of a mobile phone "shall be treated as a first offence even if the phone is switched off". For a first offence, "the examination in the course concerned shall be cancelled and the student shall be awarded the grade F in that course".

question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day. If you return after this time, you are required to sign the late-entry register kept by the security staff and provide a reason for your delay.

question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
answer: No, you cannot use an induction cooktop in your hostel room. The rules state that "the use of electric heaters, immersion rods, induction cooktops, electric kettles, irons and any appliance rated above 500 watts in hostel rooms is prohibited."

question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
answer: If you pay your fees after the due date, "a late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged on any fee paid after the due date, up to and including the last date shown in Section 2.1." Furthermore, "the late fee is capped at Rs. 1,500 for any single payment."

question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee is 31 July 2026. Please note that payments made after the due date of 15 July 2026 will attract a late fee.

question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
answer: The Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is awarded to students "whose annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 and who have a CGPA of not less than 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year or, for first-year students, not less than 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination."

question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
answer: Yes, in the event of the death of a parent, sibling, grandparent or spouse, you shall be granted bereavement leave of up to seven days, which shall be counted as attendance. You must inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application on return.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
answer: If you have outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment, you will not be issued a hall ticket for the end-semester examination. Hall tickets withheld for this reason will be released within one working day of the dues being cleared, provided the examination has not yet commenced.

question: How long can a break of study be?
answer: You may be permitted a break of study "of one semester or one academic year on medical grounds, certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean." Such a break "shall not be granted on any other ground and shall not be granted more than once during the programme."

question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
answer: You must complete all requirements of the B.Tech. programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of your first admission, failing which your name shall be removed from the rolls of the Institute.

question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to a mess rebate for your two-week absence. According to the rules, a resident absent for a continuous period of seven days or more is eligible for a rebate, provided the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of your return.

question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
answer: Every student is covered under the Institute's group medical insurance scheme for hospitalisation expenses up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year. The premium for this coverage is included in your development fee.

question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
answer: Your request for condonation of attendance shortage presents a conflict between two regulations. [AR §4.3] states that a shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances, whereas [LM §2.2] allows for the condonation of an attendance shortfall on medical grounds provided that the student's overall attendance is not less than 55 per cent.

question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
answer: There is a conflict between the regulations regarding the lowest attendance percentage that can be condoned on medical grounds. According to LM §2.2, "the shortfall may be condoned by the Dean on the recommendation of the HoD, provided that the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent." However, AR §4.3 states that "a shortage of attendance may be condoned by the Dean on medical grounds only, provided that the student's attendance in the course concerned is not less than 65 per cent," and adds that "a shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances."

question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
answer: The rulebook provides conflicting information regarding the refund amount for withdrawals before the commencement of classes. [SF §6.2] states that the tuition fee will be refunded after a deduction of a processing charge of ten per cent, whereas [FS §4.1] states that 100 per cent of the tuition fee will be refunded.

question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
answer: The regulations provide conflicting requirements for maintaining a Merit Scholarship. [AR §11.2] states that a student must maintain a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester to continue the scholarship, whereas [SF §3.1] requires a CGPA of not less than 8.0 at the end of each semester.

question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you miss an end-semester exam because of a family wedding. The closest passage covers absence from an end-semester examination due to illness.

question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student can receive a re-test for a mid-term exam missed due to a job interview. The closest passage, [EE §3.3], specifies that re-tests are granted only for absences on medical grounds supported by a medical certificate.

question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?

question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
answer: The rulebook does not address the provision of grace marks for students who fail a course by one or two marks. The closest passage covers the process of moderation, which allows for a uniform adjustment of marks across a course when the failure rate exceeds forty per cent.

question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?

question: What is the punishment for plagiarism in a project report?
answer: The use of unfair means in any evaluation is handled according to the Examination and Evaluation Regulations. Under these regulations, a first offence results in the cancellation of the examination for that course and the assignment of an F grade. Subsequent offences carry progressively harsher penalties, including the cancellation of all semester examinations for a second offence and expulsion for a third offence.
